What a release means here, and what it deliberately leaves alone.

The releasable unit is the repository: one version, everywhere. The root `package.json` is the version source — release-please bumps it, writes the root `CHANGELOG.md`, and tags `v<version>`. Nothing publishes at scaffold stage: the tag is the release, and the Go binary's version is injectable from it later via the `version` variable in `apps/api/cmd/gateway/main.go` (`-ldflags "-X main.version=<tag>"`) — the structure exists, no pipeline step consumes it yet.

`pull-request-title-pattern` overrides the default this repository would reject: release-please titles a release pull request `chore${scope}: release ${version}` where `${scope}` is the target branch — `chore(main): release 0.1.0`. CI runs commitlint on every pull request title, and `main` is not a valid scope in `commitlint.config.mjs`, so the release pull request would fail its own required check and could never merge. `workspace` is the scope that names a change owning no app, which is what a release is.

No `extra-files`: there is no second version-bearing manifest in the tree. The root `package.json` is the only one — `apps/web/package.json` stays at 0.0.0 (it is never released as a package) and the Go module carries no version field at all (its version is the tag). When a real version-bearing artifact appears, it joins `extra-files` here rather than growing a second release unit.
